heading: Equality before law
official_text: The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
plain_english_summary: Every person has the right to be treated equally by the government, public authorities, and state bodies. The state cannot arbitrarily discriminate or act unfairly.
why_relevant_explanation: Applies when government officials, public educational institutions, or state authorities subject you to arbitrary treatment, biased rules, or unjustified discrimination.
conditions_to_establish:
1. The action must be taken by 'the State' or a public/statutory authority.
2. The differential treatment must lack an intelligible differentia or rational nexus to the objective sought.
exceptions_and_limitations: Reasonable classification based on intelligible differences (e.g., affirmative action, distinct economic brackets) is constitutionally permissible.

heading: Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.
official_text: All citizens shall have the right to freedom of speech and expression.
plain_english_summary: Guarantees Indian citizens the fundamental freedom to express views, speak out, publish opinions, and share information without state censorship.
why_relevant_explanation: Relevant when facing wrongful censorship, arbitrary social media bans, or unfair suppression of peaceful public expression.
conditions_to_establish:
1. The claimant must be an Indian citizen.
2. The restriction imposed by the State must fall outside the reasonable restrictions permitted under Article 19(2).
exceptions_and_limitations: Subject to reasonable restrictions under Art 19(2) in the interests of sovereignty, integrity of India, security of the State, public order, decency, morality, or contempt of court.

heading: Protection of life and personal liberty
official_text: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.
plain_english_summary: Guarantees the inviolable right to live with dignity and personal liberty. Covers protection from illegal detention, right to privacy, clean environment, medical care, and fair trial.
why_relevant_explanation: Core constitutional safeguard against unlawful police action, illegal confinement, privacy violations (such as phone tapping or unauthorized surveillance), and arbitrary deprivation of livelihood.
conditions_to_establish:
1. Deprivation or imminent threat to life, bodily safety, dignity, or personal liberty.
2. Absence of a valid, just, fair, and reasonable procedure established by law.
exceptions_and_limitations: Lawful arrests carried out strictly in accordance with statutory criminal procedure (BNSS / CrPC) do not violate Article 21.

heading: Right to education
official_text: The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years in such manner as the State may, by law, determine.
plain_english_summary: Every child between 6 and 14 years has an unconditional constitutional right to free and compulsory elementary education.
why_relevant_explanation: Protects children against expulsion from neighborhood schools, denial of elementary admission, or demands for illegal screening or capitation fees.
conditions_to_establish:
1. Child must be between the ages of 6 and 14 years.
2. Denial of elementary schooling or barrier to basic education.
exceptions_and_limitations: Applies to elementary education (Class I to VIII) as operationalized under the RTE Act 2009.

heading: Protection against arrest and detention in certain cases
official_text: No person who is arrested shall be detained in custody without being informed, as soon as may be, of the grounds for such arrest nor shall he be denied the right to consult, and to be defended by, a legal practitioner of his choice. Every person who is arrested and detained in custody shall be produced before the nearest magistrate within a period of twenty-four hours.
plain_english_summary: If arrested, you have the right to know the exact reasons immediately, consult a lawyer of your choice, and be produced before a Magistrate within 24 hours.
why_relevant_explanation: Vital protection if stopped, questioned, or detained by police or law enforcement agencies.
conditions_to_establish:
1. Physical arrest or custody by police or state enforcement agency.
2. Denial of grounds, denial of legal access, or detention exceeding 24 hours without judicial order.
exceptions_and_limitations: Does not apply to enemy aliens or individuals detained under a valid preventive detention law.

heading: Remedies for enforcement of rights conferred by this Part
official_text: The right to move the Supreme Court by appropriate proceedings for the enforcement of the rights conferred by this Part is guaranteed. The Supreme Court shall have power to issue directions or orders or writs, including writs in the nature of habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari.
plain_english_summary: You have the constitutional right to petition the Supreme Court of India directly if any of your Fundamental Rights are infringed.
why_relevant_explanation: Used for filing Writ Petitions (e.g., Habeas Corpus for illegal detention, Mandamus to compel official duty) when basic rights are violated by the State.
conditions_to_establish:
1. Direct infringement of a Fundamental Right under Part III of the Constitution.
2. Respondent must be the State or an instrumentality of the State.
exceptions_and_limitations: Supreme Court generally directs litigants to approach the High Court under Article 226 first unless substantial national or constitutional questions exist.

heading: Power of High Courts to issue certain writs
official_text: Notwithstanding anything in Article 32, every High Court shall have power, throughout the territories in relation to which it exercises jurisdiction, to issue to any person or authority, including in appropriate cases, any Government, directions, orders or writs for the enforcement of any of the rights conferred by Part III and for any other purpose.
plain_english_summary: High Courts have wide jurisdiction to issue writs against public authorities not only for Fundamental Rights but for any unlawful or arbitrary government action.
why_relevant_explanation: Primary constitutional remedy in your respective State High Court for seeking urgent relief against arbitrary government, police, or statutory orders.
conditions_to_establish:
1. Violation of a legal or constitutional right within the territorial jurisdiction of that High Court.
2. Exhaustion of alternative effective statutory remedies or presence of fundamental arbitrariness.
exceptions_and_limitations: Discretionary remedy; will not usually substitute for ordinary civil suits involving disputed questions of private fact.

heading: Cheating
chapter: Chapter XVII - Of Offences Against Property
official_text: (1) Whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person so deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to consent that any person shall retain any property... commits 'cheating'. (4) Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property... shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
plain_english_summary: Covers financial frauds, fake schemes, scams, and deceptive delivery failures where someone took your money or goods by lying from the beginning. Punishable with up to 7 years imprisonment.
why_relevant_explanation: Applies directly to online purchase fraud where seller pocketed money without sending goods, investment scams, or deceptive transactions taking place on or after 1 July 2024.
conditions_to_establish:
1. Deception / dishonest representation by accused from the inception.
2. Inducement causing complainant to deliver money, property, or valuable security.
exceptions_and_limitations: Mere breach of contract without initial fraudulent intent is a civil dispute rather than criminal cheating.

heading: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
chapter: Chapter XVII - Of Offences Against Property
official_text: Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property to any person, or to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything which is signed or sealed, and which is capable of being converted into a valuable security, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
plain_english_summary: Classic cheating section of Indian law: penalizes deceiving a person to hand over money or property. Applies to offences committed before 1 July 2024.
why_relevant_explanation: If your fraud or payment dispute occurred prior to 1 July 2024, the FIR and charges are governed by IPC Section 420 (now Section 318(4) under BNS).
conditions_to_establish:
1. Incident date prior to 1 July 2024.
2. Fraudulent or dishonest inducement resulting in parting with property.
exceptions_and_limitations: Repealed for offences on or after 1 July 2024; successor is BNS Section 318(4).

heading: Criminal breach of trust
chapter: Chapter XVII - Of Offences Against Property
official_text: Whoever, being in any manner entrusted with property, or with any dominion over property, dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use that property, or dishonestly uses or disposes of that property in violation of any direction of law... commits 'criminal breach of trust'.
plain_english_summary: Applies when someone was trusted with your property, funds, or security deposit (e.g., landlord, agent, company) and dishonestly refuses to return or misappropriates it.
why_relevant_explanation: Pertinent when a landlord unlawfully retains your security deposit with dishonest intent, or an agent diverts entrusted money.
conditions_to_establish:
1. Entrustment of property or dominion over funds to the accused.
2. Dishonest misappropriation or refusal to return contrary to law/terms.
exceptions_and_limitations: Genuine financial disputes or bonafide claims of deduction are civil matters unless dishonest intent is proven.

heading: Stalking
chapter: Chapter V - Of Offences Against Woman and Child
official_text: (1) Any man who— (i) follows a woman and contacts, or attempts to contact such woman to foster personal interaction repeatedly despite a clear indication of disinterest... or (ii) monitors the use by a woman of the internet, email or any other form of electronic communication, commits the offence of stalking.
plain_english_summary: Protects women from repeated unwanted contact, cyber-stalking, monitoring online profiles, or persistent harassment after being told to stop. Punishable with up to 3 years imprisonment on first conviction.
why_relevant_explanation: Directly applies to online harassment, social media stalking, monitoring phone/messaging activity, and persistent unwanted digital contact.
conditions_to_establish:
1. Accused repeatedly contacted or electronically monitored the victim.
2. Complainant expressed disinterest or non-consent.
exceptions_and_limitations: Does not apply if conduct was for the purpose of preventing or detecting crime by authorized personnel or authorized by law.

heading: Word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman
chapter: Chapter V - Of Offences Against Woman and Child
official_text: Whoever, intending to insult the modesty of any woman, utters any word, makes any sound or gesture, or exhibits any object, intending that such word or sound shall be heard, or that such gesture or object shall be seen, by such woman, or intrudes upon the privacy of such woman, shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, and also with fine.
plain_english_summary: Criminalizes insulting remarks, sending lewd messages, obscene gestures, or intruding on the privacy of a woman. Punishable with up to 3 years imprisonment.
why_relevant_explanation: Directly applies when photographs are morphed, obscene comments sent via WhatsApp/Instagram, or when an individual's digital privacy is invaded.
conditions_to_establish:
1. Act, words, or electronic messages aimed at insulting a woman's modesty or intruding on her privacy.
2. Intention that the word/gesture/object be heard or seen by the woman.
exceptions_and_limitations: Requires proof of intention or knowledge that modesty would be insulted.

heading: Defamation
official_text: (1) Whoever, by words either spoken or intended to be read, or by signs or by visible representations, makes or publishes in any manner, any imputation concerning any person intending to harm... the reputation of such person, is said... to defame that person. (2) Whoever defames another shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both, or with community service.
plain_english_summary: Penalizes publishing false statements, morphed photos, or slanderous posts intended to destroy someone's personal or professional reputation. Introduces community service as a progressive penalty under BNS.
why_relevant_explanation: Applies when someone circulates defamatory posts, malicious rumors, or altered images online.
conditions_to_establish:
1. Making or publishing an imputation concerning the complainant.
2. Intention or reasonable knowledge that the imputation will harm reputation.
exceptions_and_limitations: Ten statutory exceptions, including truth published for the public good and fair criticism of public conduct.

heading: Notice of appearance before police officer
official_text: (1) The police officer shall, in all cases where the arrest of a person is not required under the provisions of sub-section (1) of section 35, issue a notice directing the person against whom a reasonable complaint has been made... to appear before him. (2) Where such a notice is issued, it shall be the duty of that person to comply with the terms of the notice.
plain_english_summary: If you receive a formal police inquiry notice (for offences punishable with up to 7 years), police cannot arrest you as long as you comply and cooperate with the notice.
why_relevant_explanation: Vital if you receive a legal notice or police summons: protects you from arbitrary arrest if you appear and cooperate with the investigating officer.
conditions_to_establish:
1. Offence punishable with imprisonment up to 7 years.
2. Recipient complies with notice terms and joins inquiry.
exceptions_and_limitations: Failure to comply or establish identity allows the police officer to proceed with arrest with court permission.

heading: Punishment for identity theft
official_text: Whoever, fraudulently or dishonestly make use of the electronic signature, password or any other unique identification feature of any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to rupees one lakh.
plain_english_summary: Penalizes stealing or misusing someone's digital identity, passwords, biometric data, UPI credentials, or OTPs without authorization. Punishable with up to 3 years imprisonment and fine.
why_relevant_explanation: Directly applies when an online scammer uses your login credentials, clones your profile, or misuses your OTP/PAN/Aadhaar details.
conditions_to_establish: 1. Fraudulent or dishonest use of unique electronic identification / password / signature of another person.
exceptions_and_limitations: Requires proof of dishonest or fraudulent intent.

heading: Punishment for cheating by personation by using computer resource
official_text: Whoever, by means of any communication device or computer resource cheats by personating, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to one lakh rupees.
plain_english_summary: Penalizes impersonating another person, bank official, government agency, or reputable business online to defraud victims.
why_relevant_explanation: Standard cybercrime section for fake courier scams, digital arrest scams, fake customer care executive fraud, and phishing portals.
conditions_to_establish:
1. Impersonation of another person/entity using computer or communication device.
2. Cheating or defrauding the victim through such impersonation.
exceptions_and_limitations: Prosecution must produce electronic evidence certificate (under Section 63 BSA 2023 / 65B IEA).

heading: Punishment for violation of privacy
official_text: Whoever, intentionally or knowingly captures, publishes or transmits the image of a private area of any person without his or her consent, under circumstances violating the privacy of that person, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to three years or with fine not exceeding two lakh rupees, or with both.
plain_english_summary: Strictly penalizes capturing, distributing, or publishing photos or videos of private body parts or private moments without clear consent.
why_relevant_explanation: Directly applies when intimate pictures or private photographs are clicked, forwarded, or uploaded online without permission.
conditions_to_establish:
1. Capturing, publishing, or transmitting the image of private area without consent.
2. Circumstances giving rise to a reasonable expectation of privacy.
exceptions_and_limitations: Consent given freely and with full information negates the offence.

heading: Unfair trade practice
official_text: 'Unfair trade practice' means a trade practice which, for the purpose of promoting the sale, use or supply of any goods or for the provision of any service, adopts any unfair method or unfair or deceptive practice including... falsely representing that the goods are of a particular standard... non-delivery or misleading advertisements.
plain_english_summary: Protects buyers when a company or e-commerce seller lies about product quality, fails to deliver ordered goods, charges above MRP, or refuses lawful refunds.
why_relevant_explanation: Governs online shopping non-delivery, received fake/damaged goods, dark patterns, and arbitrary cancellation by online platforms.
conditions_to_establish:
1. Complainant must be a 'consumer' (bought for personal use, not commercial resale).
2. Trader engaged in false representation or deceptive delivery practices.
exceptions_and_limitations: Commercial transactions for large scale resale are not covered under consumer commission jurisdiction.

heading: Manner in which complaint shall be made to District Commission
chapter: Chapter IV - Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
official_text: A complaint, in relation to any goods sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or any service provided or agreed to be provided, may be filed with a District Commission by the consumer... electronically through e-Daakhil portal or in person.
plain_english_summary: Enables consumers to file an online case (e-daakhil.nic.in) before the District Consumer Commission against deficient sellers, claiming refund and compensation for mental agony.
why_relevant_explanation: Practical legal route if an online platform, airline, hospital, or shop refuses to refund your money.
conditions_to_establish:
1. Value of goods/services and compensation claimed does not exceed Rs 50 lakh (District Commission limit).
2. Filed within 2 years from date of cause of action (Section 69 CPA).
exceptions_and_limitations: Limitation period of 2 years from date of dispute, unless condoned for sufficient cause.

heading: Payment of wages and time limit
official_text: Every employer shall pay to every employee all wages due to him within the prescribed period... where an employee has been removed or dismissed or retrenched or resigns, wages shall be paid within two working days of such removal or resignation.
plain_english_summary: Employers are legally required to disburse your salary on time, and within 2 working days if you resign or are terminated. Withholding wages is a statutory violation.
why_relevant_explanation: Directly applies when an employer withholds pending salary, final settlement, or delays compensation without justification.
conditions_to_establish:
1. Employer-employee relationship.
2. Non-payment beyond statutory deadline or unauthorized salary deductions.
exceptions_and_limitations: Deductions specifically authorized by statute (PF, ESI, Tax, court attachments) are allowed.

heading: Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee
chapter: Chapter V - Of Leases of Immovable Property
official_text: In the absence of a contract or local usage to the contrary... the lessee is bound to keep, and on the termination of the lease to restore, the property in as good condition as it was at the time when he was put in possession... The lessor is bound to disclose any latent defect and return refundable security upon peaceful handover.
plain_english_summary: Governs rental security deposits: after normal wear and tear and peaceful handover of the house/flat, the landlord is legally obligated to return the security deposit.
why_relevant_explanation: Applies when landlords make baseless deduction from your rental deposit or refuse to refund upon moving out.
conditions_to_establish:
1. Existence of tenancy/lease agreement and proof of initial deposit paid.
2. Peaceful handover with proof of key surrender and intact premises.
exceptions_and_limitations: Landlord can adjust actual damages caused by negligence beyond ordinary wear and tear.

heading: Dishonour of cheque for insufficiency, etc., of funds in the account
chapter: Chapter XVII - Of Penalties in Case of Dishonour of Certain Cheques
official_text: Where any cheque drawn by a person on an account maintained by him with a banker for payment of any amount of money to another person... is returned by the bank unpaid, either because of the amount of money standing to the credit of that account is insufficient... such person shall be deemed to have committed an offence and shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may be extended to two years, or with fine which may extend to twice the amount of the cheque, or with both.
plain_english_summary: Bouncing a cheque is a criminal offence punishable with up to 2 years imprisonment and double the cheque amount as fine.
why_relevant_explanation: Essential provision if someone gave you a payment cheque that bounced due to insufficient funds.
conditions_to_establish:
1. Cheque issued for discharge of a legally enforceable debt.
2. Cheque presented within validity period (3 months).
3. Statutory legal demand notice issued within 30 days of receiving bank bounce memo.
4. Drawer fails to pay within 15 days of receiving notice.
exceptions_and_limitations: Strict timeline: Complaint must be filed before Judicial Magistrate within 1 month after expiry of the 15-day notice window.

heading: Application for compensation
official_text: An application for compensation arising out of an accident of the nature specified in sub-section (1) of section 165 may be made by the person who has sustained the injury or by the owner of the property or where death has resulted from the accident, by all or any of the legal representatives of the deceased... to the Claims Tribunal.
plain_english_summary: Victims of road crashes or families of deceased can claim financial compensation from the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (MACT) against the offending vehicle driver, owner, and insurance company.
why_relevant_explanation: Governs motor accident claims, hospital expense recovery, loss of earnings, and permanent disability compensation.
conditions_to_establish:
1. Motor vehicle accident resulting in injury, property damage, or death.
2. Application made within 6 months of occurrence of accident (as amended in 2019).
exceptions_and_limitations: Strict 6-month limitation period introduced under Section 166(3) by the 2019 Amendment.

heading: Order for maintenance of wives, children and parents
chapter: Chapter X - Maintenance of Wives, Children and Parents
official_text: If any person having sufficient means neglects or refuses to maintain (a) his wife, unable to maintain herself, or (b) his legitimate or illegitimate child... or (d) his father or mother, unable to maintain himself or herself, a Magistrate of the first class may... order such person to make a monthly allowance for the maintenance of his wife or such child, father or mother.
plain_english_summary: A wife, minor child, or elderly dependent parents who cannot support themselves can petition a Magistrate to compel a person with sufficient means to pay regular monthly maintenance.
why_relevant_explanation: Vital provision for destitute spouses, abandoned children, and elderly parents needing swift financial sustenance.
conditions_to_establish:
1. Respondent has sufficient means.
2. Neglect or refusal to maintain claimant.
3. Claimant is unable to maintain themselves.
exceptions_and_limitations: Wife is not entitled to receive maintenance if living in adultery or without sufficient reason refuses to live with husband.
